title: Railcut synchronizer: weekly cut canonical tagging and delta changelog assembler
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a small, focused orchestration component (railcut-synchronizer) to canonicalize weekly cut metadata, generate deterministic RC tags across repos, and assemble a delta changelog draft automatically for review. The goal is to reduce manual cut drift, make RC promotion deterministic, and save ~2 engineer-hours per release cut while improving traceability for LTS channel decisions.
acceptance_criteria: railcut-synchronizer runs as a CI job and produces a canonical manifest (cut-metadata.json) for the weekly build
RC tags generated by the synchronizer are idempotent and match a reference canonicalization test on repeated runs
A draft delta changelog (markdown) is produced and attached to the release checklist PR with grouped commits by component
Console dashboard link to the weekly cut (build id + canonical manifest) is available in the release notes draft
Automation includes a dry-run mode that posts a preview in the internal release channel without mutating tags
tasks: Design manifest schema and minimal canonical fields (status: DONE)
Prototype tag canonicalizer with deterministic sorting and commit fingerprint (status: IN PROGRESS)
Integrate with GitHub actions to run on candidate branch (status: TODO)
Delta changelog assembler: group commits by component using commit footers and PR labels (status: TODO)
Add dry-run preview step to Slack/release-channel (status: TODO)
Write runbook for manual fallback and rollback tagging (status: TODO)
Add automated tests for idempotency and manifest schema (status: TODO)
notes: Decision: use a single canonical manifest file checked into a small 'release-manifests' branch rather than writing tags across many repos in first iteration to reduce blast radius
Trade-off: delaying cross-repo tag write reduces immediate automation value but dramatically lowers risk for initial rollout; plan to expand to direct tagging in Phase 2
Implementation detail: commit fingerprint will be SHA256 of concatenated (repo, sha, module, semver-intent) to avoid relying on tag timestamps
Testing: local dry-run produced identical canonical manifest on repeated runs against the same candidate commit set (3 runs validated)
Review feedback from PM (Diego Ramos): include LTS-channel hint field in manifest (low-risk) — implemented
Design review from Security (Ava Nguyen): confirmed no secret keys required; recommended RBAC for the job runner — deferred to infra task
blockers: INF-621: CI runner concurrency limits in hosted CI blocking parallel dry-runs
ENG-40211: canonical manifest schema alignment across components (dependency)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: run synchronizer in dry-run on weekly candidate branches and post changelog draft to #release-preview. Phase 2: after 2 successful dry-run weeks, flip to create release-manifests branch commits and create checklist PR. Phase 3: enable direct RC tag writing across core repos with feature flag and automated rollback job.
follow_up: Schedule a post-mortem after two weekly runs to capture mismatches and UX gaps
Add integration test that replays last 5 weeks of candidate commits into synchronizer and validates deterministic output
